title: Pricing escalation + DPA redline handoff - Aureum Logistics
summary: Kickoff between Redwood and Aureum to hand off DPA/MSA redlines, clarify SLA obligations, align on pricing escalation mechanics and pilot commercials. Customer requested clarifications around KMS, data residency, deletion windows, sub-processors, and liability caps. AE agreed to provide redlined DPA, SOC2 artifacts, and a pricing worksheet; SE to run a small benchmark for egress/per-token expectations.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-19
Time: 14:00 UTC / 07:00 PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Aureum Procurement), Maya Singh (Aureum Legal), Liam O'Connor (Aureum Platform), Sofia Reyes (Aureum Security), Ben Chao (Aureum Finance), Oliver Kim (Product), Dana Holt (Procurement)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect) ---
Jordan: quick handoff to legal on the redlines, pricing escalation and SLA mechanics, also Priya will cover the technical pilot plan and benchmark.

--- Topics ---
1) DPA redlines (retention, deletion, sub-processors)
2) MSA liability and indemnity caps
3) SLA credits & measurement windows
4) Pricing escalation and committed tiers / reserved capacity
5) KMS, VPC peering and on-prem/private deployment options
6) Pilot scope and timeline

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got a full table, so I'll try to keep this structured. This is the redline handoff call for Aureum. Priya and I will go through DPA/MSA items, SLA and pricing mechanics and then we can move into technical pilot scope.

[00:00:18] Evan (Aureum Procurement): Thanks Jordan. We got the redline from legal, Maya's made some notes, obviously a few sticking points on liability and data deletion windows.

[00:00:28] Maya (Aureum Legal): Yeah hi, thanks. I put inline comments on the DPA mostly around retention, right of deletion, and sub-processor notice. Also flagged the liability cap and the carve-outs we can't accept as-is.

[00:00:40] Jordan: Totally. On liability cap we've proposed the standard 3x fees cap in the MSA, and then exceptions for gross negligence and willful misconduct. We're open to discuss but wanted to understand Aureum's risk appetite.

[00:00:53] Maya: 3x fees is a start but our legal team is looking for a higher bucket or specific carve out limits for data breach exposure. We need to understand what insurance backing Redwood has as well.

[00:01:07] Jordan: Sure, we have CGL and cyber E&O coverage, I can share the cert of insurance. Priya, can we note anything technical that affects exposure here?

[00:01:16] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah quickly — from an infra standpoint, our hosted offering segregates customer data logically; for Aureum's regulated flows we usually recommend Dedicated or Private deployment to reduce shared-tenant blast radius. Also we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control which helps on a data access risk side.

[00:01:35] Liam (Platform): On the KMS point, is that integrated with your private offering? We need to know if keys are in our cloud KMS or Redwood's.

[00:01:43] Priya: We have both patterns. For Redwood Private you can bring your keys to your VPC through our KMS integration, or we can offer a dedicated HSM pool in Dedicated in partnership with customers. There's a slight performance delta but it's small. Also note, for Hosted we do BYOK via envelope encryption but keys sit in our KMS unless we set up a customer-managed path.

[00:02:04] Sofia (Security): And audit logs? How granular are the logs for token usage and access? We need per-request traces for compliance.

[00:02:12] Priya: We expose per-route metrics and request-level tracing in the console. For the Private deployment we can ship CloudTrail‑style logs to your S3 and maintain retention according to your policy. There might be egress cost implications for long-term retention.

[00:02:28] Ben (Finance): Egress — can we pause there? The redline flags egress fees being charged back to us unpredictably. We need clarity on how egress is priced and if it's possible to include it within committed spend.

[00:02:36] Jordan: Great point. Pricing worksheet — we proposed tiers that include compute and network assumptions. For Dedicated/reserved capacity we can absorb some egress into the committed tier; for Hosted it's harder. I'll share a pricing sheet that shows options and a model for including an egress allowance as part of committed spend.

[00:02:52] Oliver (Product): On pricing escalation, what's the escalation path if token volume grows more than expected — do we get grandfathered rates?

[00:02:59] Jordan: We usually offer a step function: initial committed tier for the pilot, then either an automatic uplift at pre-agreed thresholds or a negotiated commercial review. For long-term partners we do rate locks for a period if they commit to N months.

[00:03:14] Evan: Our procurement wants a pricing escalation clause that provides a maximum annual increase cap and a notification window.

[00:03:21] Jordan: Reasonable. Typically we agree to a 10% max annual pricing escalator on unit price unless there's a materially different product or hardware cost change, and we provide 60 days notice. I'll put that in the commercial redlines we send.

[00:03:33] Maya: Back to the DPA — retention windows: Aureum needs guaranteed deletion within 30 days of request for request logs and 90 days for model telemetry. The DPA currently says 'reasonable efforts' which is too vague.

[00:03:45] Priya: In practice, we have TTLs on KV caches and retained prefixes; we can implement a deletion workflow. The challenge is backups and log shards; guaranteed deletion is operationally possible but we need the right scoping so we don't break analytics pipelines. We can commit to 30 days for user PII request deletion and 90 days for aggregated telemetry with clear definitions.

[00:04:07] Maya: We need that in writing in the DPA. Also, sub-processors — please provide current list and a 30-day notice before onboarding new ones.

[00:04:16] Jordan: We'll include the sub-processor list and propose a 30-day notice. Our standard was 14 days but we can align to 30 for enterprise.

[00:04:25] Sofia: SOC2 Type II evidence please. We will need the report and any pen test summaries.

[00:04:30] Jordan: Yes — I'll send the SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs + a brief security pack.

[00:04:37] Liam: On SLA measurement and credits — how is uptime defined for inference? Token-level SLO is tricky. Can you map to per-route availability and 99.9 p99 latency targets?

[00:04:47] Priya: We measure per-route success rates and p50/p95/p99 latencies. For production inference SLOs we typically commit to 99.9% availability for dedicated pools and 99.5% for hosted, with credits staged for monthly windows. We can draft a measurement definition section.

[00:05:05] Maya: Crediting — legal wants an explicit formula and cap on credits. They also want to disallow credits as sole remedy for willful misconduct.

[00:05:14] Jordan: We'll include the formula (percentage downtime * monthly fee * multiplier) and cap at X% of fees, I'll propose 50% cap but open to discuss. For willful misconduct carveouts, that's standard to exclude from credits.

[00:05:29] Ben: Is there a way to instrument the pilot to reduce variance so credits are less likely? e.g., dedicated pilot window or capacity reservation?

[00:05:36] Priya: Yes — for the pilot we can provision a small Dedicated pool so you get stable latency and throughput; that reduces variability significantly. If cost is a constraint we can do a hybrid — Dedicated for critical routes, hosted for less critical ones.

[00:05:48] Evan: That solves a lot. Cost impact?

[00:05:51] Jordan: We'll show two pricing scenarios: full hosted pilot vs hybrid with Dedicated for x routes. The worksheet will show unit cost delta and recommended committed hours to hit price targets.

[00:06:03] Maya: About liability — we need a higher cap for data breach liabilities, and also contractually binding timelines for breach notification.

[00:06:10] Jordan: We can bump the cap on PII exposure claims and include 72-hour breach notification obligations. I'll have legal prepare language.

[00:06:18] Maya: 72 hours is good. Also — indemnity language around third-party claims — can we get a separation for open-source model risk? We use open models internally.

[00:06:27] Priya: Quick note on model risk: Redwood maintains a model catalog; we can provide vetting documentation and config for allowed models. If Aureum wants to bring-your-own model we can discuss indemnity scope.

[00:06:38] Liam: For pilot infra, our ops prefers VPC peering into Redwood Private vs sending traffic to Hosted. Latency-wise, which is better?

[00:06:46] Priya: VPC peering in Private gives you lowest network hop and best egress control; Dedicated in the same region is also low latency. Hosted will have slightly higher latency depending on region and routing. We'll run a baseline test.

[00:06:57] Jordan: Priya — let's note a TO‑DO: 5k token per second baseline from Aureum's EU region to their VPC, compare hosted vs dedicated vs private.

[00:07:06] Priya: noted. I'll propose test harness and a small script.

[00:07:12] Oliver: One more — data residency: some customers require EU-only processing. Are you able to pin model execution to EMEA regions?

[00:07:18] Priya: Yes, we can pin to specific regions in Private and Dedicated. Hosted has region control but not strict isolation unless you choose Private. We'll document the region pinning options.

[00:07:26] Dana (Procurement): Timeline — procurement wants to wrap commercial terms in two weeks if legal comments are resolved. Is that feasible?

[00:07:32] Jordan: If we get the redline feedback by end of week and Maya provides the must‑have language, we can target final commercial by Sep 30th.

[00:07:38] Maya: Sounds aggressive but doable. We're going to prioritize the liability and deletion clauses.

[00:07:44] Ben: For billing: we prefer monthly invoices with committed credits applied and line items for egress if outside allowance. Is that supported?

[00:07:51] Jordan: Yes — line items and credits are standard; we'll include a sample invoice breakdown in the worksheet.

[00:07:58] Evan: Any restrictions on subprocessor locations? We saw a clause about offshore subprocessors.

[00:08:04] Jordan: We can provide a list and commit to 30 days' notice for any changes; specific restrictions we usually handle case-by-case, but we can mark certain sub-processors as excluded if required by Aureum.

[00:08:15] Maya: Ok please include the sub-processor list with SOC status.

[00:08:20] Jordan: Will do.

[00:08:23] Priya: Quick technical Q from Liam — how do you handle model version pinning and rollbacks if a new model causes regression?

[00:08:30] Priya (Aureum Liam): we need rollback guarantees and traffic splitting for canaries.

[00:08:34] Priya (Redwood SE): We support version pinning and canary rollouts with automatic fallback. Also we have eval hooks to run prompt sets against new variants and a quality gate. We'll share the rollout doc.

[00:08:46] Liam: Great. Will that be available in Private?

[00:08:48] Priya: Yes, same feature set across Hosted, Dedicated, Private — consistent runtime and tooling is one of our differentiators.

[00:08:55] Evan: Alright, maybe let's talk about next steps.

[00:08:58] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to send redlined DPA and annotated MSA, SOC2 and security pack; Priya to run and share benchmarks (5k tokens baseline) and rollout doc; legal sync to be scheduled between Maya and Redwood counsel; finance to review pricing worksheet; target finalization by 2026-09-30.

[00:09:15] Maya: One ask — when you send the DPA redline, please highlight changes to deletion and sub-processor sections so we can quickly review.

[00:09:22] Jordan: Will do.

[00:09:25] Ben: Also include a sample invoice and how credits appear.

[00:09:28] Jordan: Yup.

[00:09:31] Sofia: Anything on penetration test windows? We may require a window to run our own pentest after contract signature.

[00:09:36] Jordan: We do allow customer-initiated pen tests under coordinated disclosure; we'll include the policy and process.

[00:09:42] Sofia: Good.

[00:09:45] Jordan: Ok, anyone else?

[00:09:48] Oliver: No, good.

[00:09:50] Dana: That's all from procurement.

[00:09:52] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up via email with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.

--- End of live transcript snippet (meeting continued for detailed pricing walkthrough and doc review) ---

Notes on audio quality: multiple participants, some cross talk. Occasionally 'Redwood' pronounced as 'Redwood' clear, but some acronyms were garbled (e.g., 'KMS' as 'K M S' in auto transcript).

References shared in call:
- DPA redline (uploaded to Aureum procurement drive)
- Pricing worksheet (Jordan to send link)
- SOC2 Type II and ISO certs (Jordan to send)

End meeting.
